scope: Read-only assessment of the proposed AgentRuntime runConversation consent participant; no candidate implementation approval or native execution.

findings.claim: The original shared runConversation fixture creates a real APIManager and original conversation/row request but never installs a consent responder.

The actual Host validates source arguments, current session, route, schema and deadline before asking its real owner.consent; cancellation, current context, deadline, route, scope equality and remembered grant are checked again before execution.
An existing original app test already composes the owner consent callback and answers pending requests asynchronously on MainActor.
The unchanged default is 30,000 ms. Session uses the default limits, dispatcher derives the deadline, and consent answers false at the remaining original deadline.
Retained actual local-Python and failure-recovery provider request bodies contain the original permission-denial/no-dispatch message for call-exec-python and call-valid-2.
A/B/C/malformed durations and missing responder support the same explanation, but their exact cause is not independently established from the retained excerpts examined here.
Host permission denial is permissionDenied; the higher-level invalidArguments diagnostic label must not be treated alone as evidence of malformed original arguments.

Remembering a new scope may remove older grants that share app/account/workspace/provider/tool/permissionFingerprint, even if their manifestFingerprint differs. Revoking newly created IDs alone would not restore such prior grants.
A unique conversation UUID is not a separate remembered-permission namespace: configuration stores it as namespace.space, while the approval scope uses app/account/workspace and tool fingerprints.

requirements: Keep every original scripted business argument, actual provider response, assertion, execution path, tool schema, negative case and deadline unchanged.
Use only the existing actual owner.consent.onChange/answer route. Do not replace Host.confirmInvocation, preseed grants, change policy, change production code, or substitute an executor.
Compose the prior owner callback for both pending and answered events, restore it on every exit, and keep original operation/approval event bookkeeping intact.

Build the allowlist from the exact scripted SSE function.arguments string bytes and original call ID plus alias; do not reserialize projected request.arguments. Reject duplicate/ambiguous scripted identity.

Before answering, recheck the real pending request ID and exact bytes, provider call ID, alias, actual session/conversation/scene, original row/UI run and canonical run association. A missing association must fail closed; never synthesize owner.bindings.

Answer asynchronously on MainActor, consistent with the existing participant pattern, and recheck pending/identity after suspension. This also avoids reentrant answer before the original deadline task is installed.
Do not approve unmatched, stale, cancelled or provider-only requests through this scoped Host participant. Do not count an already remembered grant as a newly answered request.

Before any allowed answer, ensure it cannot supersede an unrelated pre-existing grant under the store's exact removal predicate, or use an independently reviewed already-supported isolated test namespace. Unique conversation ID alone is insufficient.

Track exact newly created grant IDs and scopes from the synchronous before/after store state. Revoke only owned still-matching grants; preserve unrelated/pre-existing grants and verify cleanup. Never revokeAll or restore a broad stale snapshot.
Keep unmatched/cancellation cleanup and restoration explicit on normal and throwing exits, without extending original timers or leaving a responder task able to answer a later request.
limits: No fixture code, production code, tests, consent state or credentials changed by this review.
No native command, replay, test, API write, dispatch or extra GitHub poller ran for this review.
The two observed denial messages do not prove that the proposed participant will satisfy every other assertion in those six cases.
The separate supersession .unresolvedWrite at 0.549 seconds is not attributed to missing consent and requires its own causal analysis.
Actual candidate diff/API/concurrency correctness and original native acceptance remain unreviewed until source is supplied.
